subject: MAP: Benchmark variance register & close timeline for NimbleHealth
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Tan <claire@nimblehealth.com>, Tom Brooks <tom@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + performance acceptance criteria (latency/TTFT/concurrency)

Claire / Tom —

Thanks for the session yesterday. Per our MAP cadence, I’m attaching a first-draft Benchmark Variance Register and the mutual action plan workbook (MAP_NimbleHealth_20270409.xlsx). Key ask: please confirm acceptance criteria below so we can lock the evaluation plan and close timeline into the MAP.

Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- TTFT (time to first token): median <= 80ms, P95 <= 220ms on 1k token prompts in your staging VPC
- Sustained throughput: >= 150 reqs/min at 4 concurrent workers with 512-token average response
- Concurrency: system should maintain P95 latency degradation <= 30% at 8 concurrent users vs baseline
- Regression tolerance: no more than 5% token-level quality delta vs your current production baseline (BLEU/ROUGE proxy)

Test plan summary:
- Two runs: Redwood runner (our internal harness) and your runner (Locust scripts you already use) to compare tooling impact
- Model variants: rdx-13b-fp16 (baseline) and rdx-13b-8q (quantized candidate)
- Prefix caching enabled for conversational flows; KV cache replay disabled for the first pass to measure raw TTFT
- Deliverables: raw run logs, CSV of per-request latencies, and a variance register we’ll update as discrepancies are triaged

Timeline:
- April 9: finalize MAP acceptance criteria (this email)
- April 10–11: parallel benchmark runs (Redwood + Nimble)
- April 12: triage meeting to align on methodology and next steps
- April 14: MAP close / decision to proceed to Dedicated proof-of-concept or pause

I’m looping Karthik and Marissa to coordinate engine params and to own the discrepancy log. If you’re aligned on the acceptance numbers above, reply with a quick +1 and we’ll kick off the runs this afternoon.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee

Soojin —

+1 on the proposal with two small notes:
1) For TTFT we’d prefer median <= 75ms and P95 <= 200ms if feasible — our UX team has a hard threshold at ~200ms for perceived snappiness. If Redwood can commit to that on your runner, we’ll aim to parallel the same on our side.
2) We run tokenization with a different byte-pair vocab that increases token counts ~6% for our prompts. Include a column for "tokenization_ratio" in the CSV so we can normalize post-run.

We’ll start our Locust scripts today after you confirm the final run commands. I’ll also share a quick recording of our test harness (small video link in HubSpot comment).

—Claire
Claire Tan
Head of Product, NimbleHealth

All —

Running the Redwood harness now. Quick notes for the team:
- Runner config: 8 warmup threads, 60s steady-state, 4 concurrent workers by default, payloads as in MAP worksheet (avg 512 response tokens).
- Model variants loaded: rdx-13b-fp16 (baseline) and rdx-13b-8q. We’re pinning kernels to cuBLAS/flash attention for fp16; int8 path uses optimized GEMM kernels.
- Tokenization: I’ll add a tokenization_ratio column to our CSV (input_tokens_redwood / input_tokens_nimble). That should help normalize TTFT differences.

Note: early numbers show Redwood runner median TTFT ~68ms, P95 ~195ms on fp16 baseline at 4 workers (staging g4dn). Attaching run log sample.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Benchmarking Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + performance acceptance criteria (latency/TTFT/concurrency)

Soojin / team —

We finished the Locust runs this morning. Results diverge more than expected: our Locust harness shows P95 TTFT ~260ms on your fp16 baseline, and throughput at 4 concurrent workers is ~110 reqs/min. We tried the quantized candidate and saw ~12% lower median latency but bigger variance at P95.

Notes:
- We ran on a different instance family (c6i equivalent in our cloud), which likely affects system-level scheduling.
- Our harness has a 50ms client-side connection timeout that sometimes retried requests and inflated P95 — we removed retries in the second pass and saw P95 drop ~20ms.
- We pushed a copy of your run command to our CI; I’m attaching our CSV export.

We need a triage session to align tooling and explain the ±30-60ms gap. Can we do a 60-min sync tomorrow (Mon 12th) at 11am PT?

—Tom
Tom Brooks
SRE Lead, NimbleHealth
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Tan <claire@nimblehealth.com>, Tom Brooks <tom@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + performance acceptance criteria (latency/TTFT/concurrency) — triage notes and next steps

Thanks everyone for the runs and for surfacing differences. Recap and action items from today’s triage (summary for MAP register):

Findings:
- Tooling: Locust vs Redwood runner differences accounted for ~15–25ms of TTFT variance due to connection pooling and client-side retry semantics. Removing retries and aligning TCP keepalive took P95 down ~20ms in Nimble runs.
- Tokenization: Nimble tokenization_ratio averaged 1.06 across prompts; normalizing by token count explains a further ~6–10% TTFT delta. We’ll record normalized latencies in the MAP.
- Instance family: hardware differences (c6i-like vs our g4dn) explain throughput delta — recommend a follow-up where we run on a matched instance family (we can provision matching instances in your account; proxy cost to Nimble).
- Quantized model behavior: rdx-13b-8q reduces median latency but increases P95 variance; likely due to occasional kernel fallbacks under certain sequence lengths. Karthik to run a sequence-length stratified pass to confirm.

Action items and owners:
- Karthik: add tokenization_ratio column and run sequence-length stratified quantization pass (eta: 24h).
- Marissa: prepare a one-pager comparing runner differences (Locust vs Redwood harness) and recommended alignment steps; include exact run commands we used (eta: EOD Apr 12).
- Nimble (Tom): re-run Locust without client retries and with connection settings from Marissa’s doc; share full CSV (eta: Apr 13 morning).
- Soojin: update MAP_NimbleHealth_20270409.xlsx variance register with entries and next-decision checkpoint (eta: EOD Apr 12).

Decision point: if, after normalization and matched instance testing, the system meets Claire’s tightened TTFT targets (median <=75ms, P95 <=200ms) we’ll move the MAP to "green" and schedule Dedicated proof-of-concept kickoff for April 20. If not, we’ll identify specific mitigations (quantization profile changes, kernel overrides) and extend the MAP by one week.

Meeting notes and attachments are in the shared HubSpot comment and Drive link. Closing this note in the thread — I’ll update the MAP workbook with the variance register entries and owners.

Best,
Soojin
